title: Lydia
capsule: Lydia was an Iron Age kingdom in western Anatolia centred on Sardis (modern Sart, Turkey), reaching its apogee under the Mermnad dynasty that came to power around 680 BCE with Gyges. The Lydians are credited with minting the first true coinage in electrum under Alyattes (c. 610–560 BCE) and Croesus (c. 560–547 BCE), who extended Lydian power across western Anatolia to the Halys River. Croesus's misreading of the Delphic oracle's prophecy led him to attack Persia; Cyrus the Great defeated him at the Battle of Thymbra (547/546 BCE) and captured Sardis, absorbing Lydia into the Achaemenid Empire as its westernmost satrapy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Lydia's core territory is well established by ancient literary sources (Herodotus) and archaeology at Sardis, though the outer boundaries of Lydian control in eastern Anatolia before the Persian conquest are approximate.
